A1.justification: Both PDFs describe E-mem. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original LoCoMo and HotpotQA evaluations, model and routing ablations, hallucination tests, and cost/runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds architecture controls, continuous-memory tests, AMA evaluations, additional baseline comparisons and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The storage, routing, assistant reasoning and master aggregation procedure is retained. Temporal conflict resolution already appears in v1 Appendix E's timestamped examples and latest-state rule. v2 formalizes that behavior and discloses routing implementation details; optional KV caching remains supported in Appendix G.

E1.justification: v2 adds AMA evaluations covering SQL, software, games, web, embodied AI and open-world environments. It also adds continuous LoCoMo memory across five conversations and randomly shuffled HotpotQA scenarios, substantially extending the original dialogue and document-QA coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparator set remains. v2 adds a direct-read pipeline without assistants (Table 6), GPT-4o and GPT-5.1 long-context comparisons (Appendix D), and AriGraph and HippoRAG on LoCoMo (Appendix E). HippoRAG also participates in the new AMA comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds reset/no-reset evaluation across five conversations, assistant removal with concatenated contexts, random document ordering, stronger long-context model configurations, and an embedding-model substitution control. These substantially expand evaluation design while retaining the original main benchmark settings; some added-test details remain unspecified.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained model, chunk-size, routing and hallucination analyses, v2 tests whether assistants are necessary, accumulated memory causes interference, document ordering explains performance, and retriever capacity accounts for gains. The original cross-session case study is retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's random-shuffling experiment does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–5, Figure 3 and cost results retain their values. New results include direct-read versus E-mem F1 of 39.71 versus 54.17, continuous-memory F1 of 52.65, and AMA average score 69.84. HotpotQA-400/800 reasoning times change from 18.72/22.48 to 10.97/13.03 seconds without an explanation establishing the cause.

T1.justification: v2 refines the formal evidence definition into a content/absolute-timestamp tuple in Equation 8 and specifies a normalized weighted routing score in Appendix I. These are limited mathematical specification additions; the principal segmentation and reasoning equations remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: episodic context reconstruction through heterogeneous agents supports complex reasoning with strong benchmark performance and reduced token cost. The headline numerical claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 corrects the reversed vector-versus-keyword mechanism explanations in Section 4.4 and adds interpretations of the new architecture, continuous-memory, ordering and retriever controls. Storage/latency and persistent-memory privacy qualifications expand the discussion, while the original latency–fidelity trade-off and application positioning remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository address, AMA data location, embedding-model identities, threshold/normalized-weighted routing details, and quantified disk/VRAM requirements with sequential execution options (Appendices G and I). These substantially improve technical disclosure, although numerical routing thresholds and weights remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The related-work section and bibliography largely retain the same works; Zheng's roadmap receives a publication update. New appendix discussions add limited positioning against AriGraph/HippoRAG and powerful single-model long-context systems, including the claim that smaller models can compete with GPT-5.1.

P1.justification: v2 revises introductory and concluding prose, standardizes terminology, expands temporal explanations, updates author/header text and adds an Impact Statement. Caching discussion moves from Section 3.5 to Appendix G, and appendices are reorganized; most existing narrative and prompt text remains.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation substantially expands with direct-read, continuous-memory, AMA, stronger long-context, graph-baseline and document-order comparisons. Figures 1–2 receive terminology/notation edits, while Figures 3–4 retain their content. Existing cost/runtime tables and the algorithm are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The direct-read control, continuous-memory test and AMA evaluation substantially address gaps in v1's empirical support for the architecture and its intended use cases. Additional baselines and routing/storage disclosures improve assessability. Sparse new-test protocols, unexplained runtime revisions and inconsistent repeated RAG values—such as 16.87 in Appendix E versus 23.23 in Table 1 for open-domain performance—limit the gains, but do not outweigh the substantial strengthening of validation.
